releases.name: OpenCode Vitals 0.2.0
releases.body:
## [0.2.0] - 2026-10-10

Arabic text reads correctly in messages and the prompt box — folded into the same
plugin, the same renderer copy and the same launcher entry as the readout, so it is
one plugin instead of two.

### Added

- **Arabic text direction.** The renderer copy now also carries `arabic.css` and
  `arabic.js` beside the readout:
  - `unicode-bidi: plaintext` and `text-align: start` on message blocks (assistant
    replies, user messages, compaction, retries) and the composer, so each block
    reads and aligns by its own content;
  - `direction: ltr` on code, diffs, paths and shell output, so those are never
    reordered inside an Arabic paragraph;
  - `dir="auto"` on message blocks, so an Arabic block becomes genuinely
    right-to-left and OpenCode's own `:dir(rtl)` rules mirror its layout, while an
    English block beside it stays left-to-right.
- The three injected files (`vitals.js`, `arabic.css`, `arabic.js`) are copied and
  hashed together, so a change to any of them reaches a copy whose app has not
  moved. A copy missing any of them is no longer treated as ready, and a sync
  rebuilds it.

### Measured

- 493 checks, up from 485.


---

Upgrade: `npx opencode-vitals install`

releases.name: OpenCode Vitals 0.1.18
releases.body:
## [0.1.18] - 2026-10-10

The readout comes back by itself when the server it deferred to goes away.

### Fixed

- **The readout could stay dark until the whole service was reloaded.** When the
  plugin's own bind was refused with `EADDRINUSE` it latched "the launcher host
  owns the port" and never tried again — but the host lives only as long as the
  window it opened, so once it exited nothing served, the running window lost the
  page it was loading, and the row vanished. A liveness probe now checks every few
  seconds whether the port actually answers; if it does not, the plugin stops
  trusting the host and takes the port back. The probe waits five seconds rather
  than half a second, because a server that is briefly busy is not a server that
  is gone.
- A refused bind no longer leaves a server object behind that made the plugin
  think it was serving — which is also what kept the probe above from running.
- The launcher host's own readiness probe uses the same five-second patience.

### Measured

- 485 checks, up from 482.


---

Upgrade: `npx opencode-vitals install`

releases.name: OpenCode Vitals 0.1.17
releases.body:
## [0.1.17] - 2026-10-10

An audit of the measurement and the installer. Nothing here changes what the
readout looks like; it changes what it says, and it keeps the plugin from being
able to stop OpenCode.

### Fixed

- **The plugin could hang after 51 sessions.** The in-memory session table was
  evicted with `Map.delete(values().next().value)` — a value where a key is
  required — so every eviction was a no-op and the `while` around it spun
  forever the moment the cap was reached, blocking the event loop. It evicts by
  key now. This was the most serious finding of the audit and had no test.
- **An interrupted stream lost the time it streamed before the gap.** A silence
  longer than 30 seconds under one message resets the stream span so the gap is
  not counted; resetting `first` also threw away everything streamed before it,
  which made a reconnect look fast instead of slow. The earlier stretch is banked
  now, so only the gap is dropped.
- **A session's tok/s was inflated by its subagents' tokens.** Delegated tokens
  are counted in the parent's totals but arrive with none of the parent's stream
  time; the rate was recomputed from those totals on the parent's next own turn,
  dividing the subagent's tokens by the parent's seconds. The rate is taken from
  the session's own tokens and time now, while the totals still show the delegated
  work.
- **A second subagent credit to a parent with no turn of its own was dropped from
  the published totals.** Two such snapshots rank equal on `turns` alone, and the
  tie preferred the older on-disk one. Snapshots carry a revision counter now, so
  the newer credit wins.
- **A malformed request target could crash the readout server.** `new URL` throws
  on some request lines (`//..%2f..`, `///`) and the throw was uncaught, in the
  plugin host. A bad target is a 400 now and the server stays up.
- **A shell that vanished between the check and the open was an uncaught stream
  error.** The document is served through the same guarded helper the assets use.
- **Registering the package never removed a copy already in the plugin
  directory.** The check read `stale.installed`, a field `describeExisting` does
  not return, so both shapes stayed and the plugin loaded twice. The copy is
  removed directly — not through `uninstall`, which would have unregistered the
  package just added.
- **Every successful install printed "OpenCode has X, not X".** `register()` was
  called without the version being installed, so its comparison was skipped and
  the state was always reported as outdated.
- **Ordinary session lifecycle events were counted as unknown measurements.**
  `session.status`, `session.created`, `session.renamed` and seven others landed
  in `unknownEventTypes` and produced a warning, the exact noise the unknown-event
  mechanism exists to avoid. They are named as ignored now.
- A reload of one location leaked its marker timer and readout-pool entry, since
  its cleanup is not run when OpenCode runs setup again.
- A quoted `Exec` in the system launcher hid the binary (the quotes stayed on the
  path), and a binary with a space was written unquoted into the entry this plugin
  writes.
- `OPENCODE_VITALS_PORT` was used unvalidated: an empty or junk value made the
  launcher entry point the window at a port nothing could listen on.
- The launcher host reported every application exit as success. It forwards the
  application's own exit code now.
- A slow server could stack concurrent polls, because `setInterval` does not await
  an async callback. A poll now skips while one is already in flight.
- The published totals file grew one entry per session forever; it is capped at
  200, ranked so the work that got furthest survives.
- `session-totals.json` was written through a plain object; a `__proto__` session
  id could have rewired it instead of being stored.
- Uninstall now also removes a stale storage lock and a half-written atomic temp
  file, and honours an explicit status directory

releases.name: OpenCode Vitals 0.1.16
releases.body:
## [0.1.16] - 2026-10-10

An OpenCode update no longer needs a second launch to open the window.

### Fixed

- **Updating OpenCode could still show "ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED".** The launcher
  host is started by the launcher entry and lives as long as the window. When the
  app closed for an update, the host closed with it — and the update relaunches
  the app a moment later, against a port the restarted service had not bound yet.
  The host now keeps serving through a grace period after the window closes, so
  the relaunched window meets a server; it leaves only if nothing comes back.

### Measured

- 454 checks, up from 453.


---

Upgrade: `npx opencode-vitals install`

releases.name: OpenCode Vitals 0.1.15
releases.body:
## [0.1.15] - 2026-10-10

A cold start no longer greets the window with a refused connection.

### Fixed

- **The first launch after a reboot could show "ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED".** The
  readout server runs inside OpenCode's background service, and the desktop
  window is opened before that service has finished starting — on a cold start
  the window asked for `http://127.0.0.1:8971/index.html` while nothing was
  listening, and the window did not open at all. The launcher entry now starts a
  small readout host first, using the app's own binary run as Node, so a server
  is listening before the window is. The plugin's own server binds the same port,
  and `reusePort` lets the two share it — so an OpenCode update, which restarts
  the service the plugin lives in, cannot leave the window without one. If there
  is no copy to serve, the window is opened without a readout rather than against
  a port that answers nothing.

### Changed

- The package ships `host.mjs`, and the launcher entry runs it instead of the app
  directly. It needs no runtime the machine might not have: it runs as Node
  through the app's own Electron binary.

### Measured

- 453 checks, up from 439.


---

Upgrade: `npx opencode-vitals install`
